items.item: No generated face, avatar or synthetic human in any frame
items.note: Forty-six frames, one every ten seconds. Type, charts and the corner; no figure appears anywhere in the film.
No texture is used at all. Every frame is the paper room: a kinetic card, a chart, a figure, or a chapter card.

items.item: Every number on screen traces to a model run, and demo data is labelled
items.note: Every figure is drawn from facts.json and run.json through the reveal loop; nothing is typed into a scene. The TARNHOLLOW DEMO DATA chip is on every frame.

items.item: Charts are Manim scenes driven by engine output, not hand-rebuilt
items.note: Waterfall reads the month's revenue, fees, landed cost, ads and net; CashCone reads the horizon's own paths, band, wire ticks and trough; Newsvendor reads the service-level cost curve for TH-CHEKNI-08. All three are the scenes/ classes in the site's chart grammar.

items.item: Every chart builds progressively and carries an annotation
items.note: Axes and labels, then the data, then the annotation: the waterfall's bars left to right to the blue net (f-006, f-007), the cone's band then its wire ticks then the trough dot labelled $95,201 on day 13 (f-010 to f-023), the newsvendor's short-one-unit line then the one-unit-too-many line then the fractile (f-028 to f-030).

items.item: Room tone, data ticks, transition SFX and a ducking bed
items.note: mix.json: room tone at -48 dB, eleven ticks, two whooshes, bed-elevenlabs.mp3 at -32 dB ducking to -20 dB, SFX from ElevenLabs sound generation. QA reads no silence over a second anywhere in the film.

items.item: A publishable voice, disclosed as what it is
items.note: voice is "library": the ElevenLabs library voice the founder chose on 2026-10-04 (content/assets/voice.json), which PREMIUM-STANDARD accepts as amended. The description does not exist yet, so qa.json reports disclosure_in_description as null; that is the describe step's check.

items.item: Cut to VISUAL_SPEC §4, and nothing frozen over four seconds
items.note: qa.json: 51 cuts, mean interval 8.89 s, longest 24.6 s, inside the thirty a chart build may hold; no frozen run in any scene clip. This failed first at 36.73 s and was fixed at the source, not waived: the chart's hold read only the gap in front of it, so the first chapter spent its whole build clock drifting up to a run of six figures three seconds apart and then had no legal cut between any of them. The hold is now told where the run it leads into ends and takes its cut while a window exists (scenes/base.py, cluster_end).

items.item: Subtitles burned in, legible, never boxed
items.note: Coverage 1.0, transcript match 0.959. Inter Display in ink with a thin paper outline, two lines, centred over a wide bottom margin; no box. The picture keeps out of the band on every frame.

items.item: The style lock is written and followed
items.note: content/assets/style-lock.json, locked from V01 on 2026-10-05. Paper, ink, one blue, Inter Display at the stage's sizes; the two chapter cards are the spec's hairline and title. Nothing in these frames departs from it.

items.item: One blue element per frame, and blue only on money and the leak
items.note: Blue falls on the waterfall's net bar, the cash line and band, the newsvendor's short-one-unit curve, and the spoken money figures ($95,201 at f-020, $322,319 at f-027, $61,358 at f-034, $31,500 at f-041). Every other callout, label and card is ink; no red and no green anywhere. The same thing V04's review left for the founder holds here: a frame carrying a blue money figure over a blue chart line has blue in two places, which the house grammar allows but only he can settle for the series.

items.item: No gradient, glow, halo or vignette; hard cuts only
items.note: None in any frame. Transitions are hard cuts; the only motion inside a shot is the drift the spec asks for.

items.item: At most three text blocks per frame, captions small and dim
items.note: The busiest frames are the chart ones: heading, then at most two callouts in the right column, with the burned-in subtitle counted separately. The older callout of the pair steps back from blue to ink.

items.item: Charts have direct labels, a demo label, no legend and no grid
items.note: Hairline axes, three or four numbers on each, every line and bar named where it sits. No legend and no gridlines anywhere.

The figures are legible and correctly placed, but two of them are read out in a sentence that does not survive the substitution. min_p5_day's value is "13 days" and largest_wire_day's is "0 days", and the script writes the word day in front of each: the screen and the narration both say "bottoms out on day 13 days" (f-001), "leaves on day 0 days", "in the bank on day 0 days" (f-022), "goes out on day 0 days" (f-031) and, as a full display card, "Where the line dips lowest is your own day 13 days" (f-038). The chart's own annotation gets it right ($95,201 on day 13, f-023), which is what makes the narration read as a bug. The fix is in the script and its facts, not in a scene: either the sentences drop the word day, or the facts carry a day index without the unit for the sentences that already supply it.

items.item: The narration describes the picture that is actually on screen
items.note: The script says "with every supplier wire as a red tick" (script.md line 34). The ticks render in ink, correctly: VISUAL_SPEC §3.1 (2026-10-04) retires red and green outright and the film carries no red pixel. The line is a leftover from the navy-and-amber palette, as is the THUMBNAIL line on script.md line 2 ("{{min_p5}} in amber ... the supplier wires as red ticks"), which the thumbnail step will read next. Naming a colour the viewer cannot see is small, but it is the narration telling him something untrue about his own screen.

notes: Sixteen items, fourteen passing. The render itself is clean and the two program failures were fixed at the source: the cadence defect in the chart's hold (now 51 cuts, longest stretch 24.6 s) and nothing frozen anywhere. Both failures left are in the approved script, so neither can be fixed inside this step: the script is at review == approved, and changing a word of the narration means re-recording it, re-timing it and re-rendering the scenes against it. The step is blocked on the founder re-approving a corrected script. The corrections are exactly two, and neither touches a figure or a claim: drop the word day in front of {{min_p5_day}} and {{largest_wire_day}} (or give the facts a day index without its unit), and drop the colour from "as a red tick" and from the thumbnail line.
